summary: Opening recap follows Abby's unarmed defiance of the Triarch's blockade into a new physical corridor anomaly the Triarch did not cause.
panelPlan: One-page title/recap splash: from the recently reopened Gate, small recognizably Shard ships that refused the blockade share space with civilian hulls passing into a physically ordinary Calm Corridor.
The reciprocal corridor is clean, navigable space, not a glowing portal. An almost unnoticed delayed double-reflection lies at the far end, outside the reach of political action.
Reserve a readable caption field. No invented labels, symbols with writing, or diagrams that appear to name the anomaly.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: REX FLEET #7

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: PREVIOUSLY IN REX FLEET...

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Triarch ordered the civilian routes closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Abby Saville refused.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Seven Shard captains opened the lane without firing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Civilian ships crossed. The blockade failed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beyond the Gate, the Calm Corridor still measured safe.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the reflections began.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening recap. The Triarch exploits the anomaly later; it did not create it. Show distinct Shard and civilian ships with correct existing vessel design where named. Preserve captions exactly; no unscripted environmental text.

summary: A genuinely stable reciprocal-field corridor carries routine survey traffic; one delayed reflected position is the first sign that its images cannot all be trusted.
directionInline: Show trained survey crews and ordinary anchor-beacon navigation under nominal reciprocal gap, shear, and timing. Nothing indicates a conventional field failure. The anomaly begins as one subtle positional reflection whose timing disagrees with a real hull's maneuver. Do not show a colorful tunnel, magical mirror portal, or an invented second physical ship.
panelPlan: Open wide on recognizable, restrained Calm Corridor geometry with survey hulls transiting in ordinary formation; anchor beacons and simple vector graphics remain nominal.
Convey calm through unhurried real spacecraft and consistent measurable lanes rather than abstract spectacle.
A small reflected glint trails a survey vessel's corrected heading an instant too late; no one has yet inferred a cause.

summary: Survey crew members witness an impossible delayed reflection while the corridor remains inside its familiar safety envelope; they secure the observations instead of guessing at an explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain
dialogueInline.text: Reciprocal gap steady. Maintain the survey run.

dialogueInline.speaker: Technician
dialogueInline.text: My reflection finished moving after I stopped.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain
dialogueInline.text: Keep your hands where they are. Record the return.

directionInline: The technician's reflection lags a completed real movement while ordinary shear, anchor coupling, and gap remain nominal. A second real survey hull responds to an unverified displayed return and nearly approaches another actual hull; the shipboard log therefore contains an authentic near miss later edited by Fear. The captain orders unaltered evidence preserved. Apparent duplicates are optical/positional returns, not independent physical crew.
panelPlan: An ordinary survey bridge with nominal graphical instruments and an uninterrupted real transit track.
In an instrument reflection the technician's previous reach finishes visibly later than the real reach; the reader can compare poses within one panel.
On the recorded external feed, a second real survey hull begins an unnecessary correction toward that false contact and barely keeps clearance.
The captain holds steady and orders the crew to capture the raw returns rather than declare a cause.

summary: Jex refuses to abandon three medical-supply windows on uncertain evidence; Naomi insists he tell captains what the survey recorded rather than sell yesterday's certainty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Those three windows brought in the last medical freight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The survey recorded a contact it couldn't verify.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Cancel the windows and the medicine stays here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then give every captain the footage. Don't call it a clean crossing.

directionInline: In Veil Market's back room, Jex has supply allocations and an actual backlog on his slate beside uncut survey footage. The three windows carry genuine civilian stakes as well as income. Naomi makes him expose the uncertainty rather than pretending it can be ignored. Jex flags the windows as unverified but, for now, leaves them available for informed captains; his visible reluctance is about people and money. Halev is not present.
panelPlan: Jex works a practical route board with three live windows and awaiting medical shipments; the survey footage runs alongside them without invented labels.
Naomi isolates a verified real hull and a late apparent return; their disagreement is grounded in medicine waiting for passage.
Jex reluctantly sends the complete survey recording with the window advisories and leaves the booking positions live. Neither has won the argument.

summary: Jia isolates a measurable 1.7-second delay between an actual ship maneuver and a second observed return while ruling out a conventional inversion failure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jia
dialogueInline.text: Gap and shear are normal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jia
dialogueInline.text: Manual burn. The real hull changes vector. The return follows one-point-seven seconds later.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: A bad inversion?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jia
dialogueInline.text: The ship's field never left tolerance. The delay is in what we're seeing.

directionInline: Jia uses standard Academy reciprocal-field models and original timecoded survey samples, without turning a correlation into an explanation. Venn's concern is practical; Selene separately preserves sources and competing interpretations through work at an ordinary research console, not mystical archiving. End without a knowing joke or premature name for the effect.
panelPlan: On Thunderbreak command, compare an ordinary Academy operating envelope to nominal gap/shear from the live recording.
Show real survey hull turning after a manually ordered burn, then apparent return trailing the old line.
Jia isolates the one-point-seven-second lag. Venn studies the physical ship track; Selene separately retains unmodified measurements, none of them claiming a mechanism.

summary: Continuing the prior issue's evacuation, Tess clears the last adults from Tal Corvus before checking a delayed wall reflection; no one is endangered for the sake of spectacle.
settingText: TAL CORVUS — SERVICE LIFT EXIT / CIVILIAN TRANSFER — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Keep the transfer ramp clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Evacuee
dialogueInline.text: The reflection didn't move when I did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I saw it. Go with the others.

directionInline: Continue, do not restart, the Issue 6 warren evacuation: survivors have already left the narrow exit and are boarding the transfer lift and skiffs. One adult evacuee sees a delayed hand reflection in a metal service panel. Tess moves people out first, then checks the intact plate with her gloved hand without breaking or dispelling anything. Do not use a child or make the anomaly a physical attacking creature.
panelPlan: Adult evacuees from the already-cleared passage move toward a transfer lift and practical refugee boarding ramp.
One adult's hand withdraws, but its image persists briefly on the panel; another adult assists an older passenger with belongings.
Tess gets the last person through before examining the intact reflective panel. No supernatural material shatters under her glove.

summary: Billie demands the actual results of a failed Shard weapons test and stops wasting ammunition on apparent targets that register no confirmed impact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: What did the impact scopes record?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Clean discharge. No confirmed strike, debris, or field change.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then we're firing at a picture. Stop the tests. Send me the raw run.

directionInline: Billie reviews transmitted Shatterforge test recordings, not a live battle. Weapons have been fired at an apparent anomaly return, but no measurable target interaction can be verified. Her impatience drives an evidence-based decision that costs her the obvious weapons answer. Do not give her a generic pirate tantrum or suggest shots occur in the later civilian convoy.
panelPlan: On recognizable Ashfang command, Billie studies two simultaneous feeds: a real weapon firing on a test range and a false contact that provides no confirmed physical impact.
The officer shows an unchanged measured field plot after the shot; the result is disappointing but specific.
Billie cancels further firing and requests the untouched trial data. Her expression is frustrated, not stupid or heroic.

summary: The Fear Mask uses a real near miss to demand centralized transit certification, cutting away successful periods without having to invent the hazard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: Most of the survey run was uneventful.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: The near miss was real.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: The recovery was real too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: Broadcast the near miss. Demand clearance before the next Shard departure.

directionInline: Within the Shard Arena Vault, Fear sees a genuine near-collision buried in a mostly uneventful survey record, removes the stable sections and observed recovery, and publishes only authentic alarming footage. The institutional aim is to reclaim authority over Shard route permissions after Abby's captains defied the blockade. The political weapon is misleading selection and a defensible-sounding safety claim, not a manufactured cosmic effect or cartoon panic slogans. No invented text on broadcasts.
panelPlan: The full uncut survey recording shows many normal moments and one actual close approach caused by unreliable apparent contacts.
The emissary keeps the benign and recovery segments visible while Fear selects only the alarming seconds; keep the act of selective editing physically clear.
The chosen clip propagates on graphical public feeds, accompanied by no invented headlines. A Shard clearance emblem on a control console ties it to authority rather than theatrical villainy.

summary: Sunlash and Gravefire escort civilian and medical skiffs into a corridor whose risk is known but whose alternative routes remain blocked or unverified.
directionInline: The convoy decision follows P03: civilian passengers and urgently needed medicine must leave Tal Corvus and reach receiving berths; available alternatives are closed or unverified. Sunlash provides Verge escort discipline; Gravefire is a distinct Shard cutter. Neither is redesigned. The skiffs initially use synchronized burns because that has previously kept them within predictable convoy separation. Duplicate reflections appear before the danger is understood. No gunfire occurs.
panelPlan: A clear wide establishes the actual escort geometry: Sunlash, Gravefire, and separate refugee skiffs, with medicine among the visible civilian cargo.
A small inset shows a real skiff carrying ordinary passengers and medical cases, giving a human reason for entering this imperfectly understood route.
The escorts and skiffs correct together. Similar delayed apparent returns begin sharing their timing, with normal reciprocal transit continuing beneath the phenomenon.

summary: Naomi is briefly struck by the beauty of the reflections, then notices that a refugee skiff has started correcting toward a contact nobody can verify.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: Skiff Three is correcting toward an unconfirmed return.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Give them our real position. Keep them clear of that contact.

directionInline: On Sunlash bridge, the quiet strange beauty is conveyed by Naomi's involuntary glance and the canopy imagery, not a staged joke about finding danger pretty. She immediately attends to the actual skiff that may be reacting to a false plot. Only real maneuverable hulls can collide; apparent duplicates are not established as physical vessels.
panelPlan: Naomi watches restrained mirrored lights beyond Sunlash; her expression briefly registers wonder.
A practical pilot points out a real refugee skiff shifting toward a displayed but unverified contact.
Naomi marks Sunlash's confirmed hull vector for the skiff and remains in command.

summary: Tess keeps Gravefire focused on confirmed civilian hulls as a lagging apparent duplicate tempts the crew to trust its position.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crew
dialogueInline.text: The second Gravefire kept our old heading.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then it's not our position. Stay on the skiffs.

directionInline: Gravefire's ordinary instruments identify its own real vector while a lagging reflected image repeats the earlier vector. The crew member's anxiety is credible, but no image looks back, predicts the future, or behaves as a creature. Tess's attention remains on refugee spacing.
panelPlan: Inside Gravefire command, distinct Shard red-marked flight equipment frames a verified real vector plot.
A second apparent Gravefire remains on an obsolete trajectory after the cutter corrects; the timing difference is visually legible.
Tess checks the civilian skiffs rather than chasing the visually seductive duplicate.

summary: Jia sees synchronized burns correlating with unreliable duplicated returns just as two real skiffs lose safe clearance; Venn asks Naomi for a live field test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jia
dialogueInline.text: The late returns tighten whenever the convoy burns together. Guidance is treating them as hulls.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Actual separation?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jia
dialogueInline.text: Two real skiffs are converging. The formation plot still calls it clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Naomi, can you split their timing?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I can. Keep each ship's navigation live; take them off formation sync.

directionInline: Thunderbreak physically contains only Jia and Venn. Naomi is on Sunlash, appearing solely on a ship-to-ship video or audio communications display. Establish the hazard from two confirmed real hulls drifting toward collision while their automated formation display is contaminated by apparently valid returns. Jia has a testable correlation, not a solved physical model. Venn accepts Naomi's practical judgement; nobody shuts down anchors or all navigation displays.
panelPlan: Jia shows separate unambiguous verified hull positions and duplicated apparent contacts as the convoy executes simultaneous control inputs.
A paired physical-space exterior inset makes the two real skiffs' decreasing separation visible despite a deceptively clear formation plot.
Venn opens a live channel to Naomi. Naomi, framed explicitly on Sunlash's communications display, agrees to separate timings while retaining local ship controls.

summary: The convoy begins independent timed maneuvers while keeping local navigation and anchor monitoring intact; apparent echoes briefly follow the obsolete common solution.
directionInline: The correction is a risky hypothesis being tested in real time, not a universal cure. Following Naomi's communicated instruction, one escort burns ahead of count, Gravefire holds off-axis, one skiff coasts, and another corrects late; all retain their own navigation, collision lookout, and reciprocal-field coupling. Real skiffs begin separating safely. Apparent returns persist along prior common vectors before losing their misleading coherence. No magic, vanishing physical ships, or firing.
panelPlan: Use a wide established geometry from P08: civilian hulls are nearly converging under the false formation solution.
A staggered series of tight inserts show different real engines and human pilots executing different timings; their vectors become visually distinguishable.
A large exterior panel shows confirmed real hulls separating as delayed apparent returns continue on obsolete headings. Keep the uncertainty visible rather than portraying the anomaly as defeated.

summary: From their separate ships, Naomi and Tess coordinate offset burns that disentangle real convoy tracks without extinguishing individual navigation.
settingText: INT. SUNLASH — BRIDGE / LIVE COMMS TO GRAVEFIRE

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Two, hold the burn. Skiff Three, coast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire's off your count. The real skiffs are separating.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Keep them on separate clocks until we're clear.

directionInline: Naomi is physically on Sunlash. Tess remains physically aboard Gravefire and is visible or audible only over communications. Pilots use local nav and discrete ship-to-ship calls; do not depict visual hand-signaling across spacecraft canopies. This overlaps P12's early maneuver and P14's continuing cabin response. Any brief dry warmth should arise naturally from competence, not filler banter.
panelPlan: Naomi uses tactile Sunlash flight controls and a real-time convoy channel, not a holographic command spectacle.
An inset of Gravefire's separate bridge shows Tess confirming her actual burn timing over comms.
Return to a real-skiff separation readout recovering clarity, with the reported physical positions agreeing with exterior geometry.

summary: As the improvised maneuver continues, Tess makes cabin crews secure frightened adults while clearing the pilot channel for the final separation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Cabin crews, get everyone seated. Use the passenger channel; pilots keep the flight frequency.

directionInline: This action runs concurrently with P12–P13, before the last skiff has cleared. From Gravefire Tess reaches an adult cabin lead in a refugee skiff; one distressed adult passenger is pulling toward a viewport, while another helps secure fragile medical freight. Let their distinctive worried expressions give weight to the choice to restrict noisy passenger chatter. Tess is not physically inside the skiff, and she does not deliver a calming-mantra speech.
panelPlan: Within a real refugee skiff, adults crowd a viewport as false reflections distort their sense of distance.
An adult cabin lead secures people and fragile medical cases while a passenger reluctantly takes a seat; Tess's practical instruction comes over a modest working speaker.
Return to Gravefire: the flight frequency is clear for the pilots still making staggered, risky corrections.

summary: The real convoy hulls recover verified separation and exit the corridor using an unproven but effective local workaround; the echoes remain unexplained.
directionInline: The last real refugee skiff clears the corridor with safe measured separation; its apparent return continues for a moment along the earlier vector and grows too faint to track. The observed effect has not been destroyed, named, or explained. The ships do not fire here and have not fired anywhere in this convoy. Preserve the established actual ship positions and unchanged hull condition.
panelPlan: Wide: unmistakably real Sunlash, Gravefire, and refugee hulls move apart on independent vectors toward the receiving berths.
A small insert contrasts the last confirmed real skiff with one late apparent return following the obsolete common line.
Hold on the last real skiff safely clearing; relief is visible in human pilots as much as on instruments. No cosmic explosion or triumphant defeat effect.

summary: Jex cancels and refunds the three unverified windows that helped feed the convoy, accepting a costly shortage and publishing the limits of what the crossing proved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Close all three Calm Corridor listings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: That includes every paid booking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Credit them. Send the crews' original recordings with the cancellation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: The medical shipments behind them have no route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Then we tell the buyers that too.

directionInline: At the Veil Market council hall, Jex watches the convoy's verified arrival and acts on the disturbing operating evidence. He loses real income and strands genuine medical supply traffic. His scribe is not a punchline: they bring him the cost and stranded orders. Jex records the uncertainty openly rather than deferring indefinitely to a scientist's permission or performing virtue. Connect this outcome to Issue 8's unresolved empty shelves.
panelPlan: Jex receives confirmed arrival pictures but can still see unverified route returns in the raw run.
He cancels his three windows and authorizes actual customer credits, with visible cargo reservations becoming unusable through purely graphical slate changes.
The scribe shows awaiting orders and medical freight that cannot now move. Jex does not erase those losses with a joke.

summary: Fear turns one successful crossing into a dispute over whether Abby's captains may authorize routes without Triarch certification, setting up the next challenge to their legitimacy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: The convoy made it. Their captains are circulating the telemetry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: One crossing is not a safe operating standard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: Saville's seven captains won't surrender their departure clearances.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: Then challenge who has the right to issue them.

directionInline: In the Arena Vault, the Triarch sees real successful arrival footage and credible risks remaining from the same event. Their response is to dispute Shard-controlled route certification and the authority of Abby's captains, not to claim the physical anomaly was their creation or declare science settled. They aim to rebuild institutional command through legitimacy, opening a road to Oren Pike's spectacle in Issue 8 without showing that duel yet. Fear Mask remains a distinct political person in an established mask, not supernatural.
panelPlan: The uncut crossing evidence now includes a genuine successful arrival alongside earlier near-collision telemetry.
The emissary shows a graphical map of Shard captain clearances: seven captains remain aligned with Abby. No invented words or banners.
Fear chooses a challenge to their authority, seen in the human response of the emissary rather than a theatrical villain pose.

summary: At the receiving berth, undamaged escorts arrive in a ragged but measurable formation and civilian passengers unload needed medical cargo while still looking back for their copies.
settingText: EXT. CALM CORRIDOR RECEIVING BERTH — NIGHT
directionInline: The actual escorts and skiffs dock after P15's exit, with no invented scorch marks or repairs. Their staggered approach is the visible cost of relinquishing formation synchronization. Adult refugees disembark as workers unload genuine medical cases. Several people turn toward the corridor and find no remaining visible copies; relief does not make them certain that later crossings will be safe.
panelPlan: Wide berth arrival: Sunlash, Gravefire and each real skiff approach in visibly imperfect spacing with correct established hull silhouettes.
Medium civilian-scale panels: adults help one another disembark and move medical cases into waiting workers' hands.
A survivor glances back toward apparently ordinary open space. Their apprehension persists even after reaching safe flooring.

summary: Tess meets a surviving adult she evacuated earlier; the person who made the crossing asks about the people still waiting behind, preventing the issue from mistaking one escape for general safety.
settingText: INT. REFUGEE RECEIVING BERTH — GRAVEFIRE GANGWAY — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Evacuee
dialogueInline.text: There are three more skiffs waiting at Tal Corvus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: How many people?

directionInline: This adult is the same evacuee who saw the delayed reflection on P05, now safe beyond the corridor. Tess leaves Gravefire only after the last refugee skiff is confirmed docked. Their exchange occurs among ordinary unloading adults and medical freight; not a mystical moment, coffee joke, inspirational speech, or a claim that the next transit is safe. Tess's practical question recognizes the immediate civilian problem that survives the science experiment. No chalk arrow prop appears without prior cause.
panelPlan: From Gravefire, Tess checks the last actual docking indicator before approaching the receiving gangway.
The previously seen adult evacuee, carrying familiar modest luggage, speaks to Tess while other survivors unload cases nearby.
A close two-shot holds on Tess asking for the number still waiting. End on an unresolved human responsibility rather than a triumph pose.

summary: Closing teaser links the corridor's unresolved safety and authority questions to Pike's public challenge against Tess, without recounting the entire prior rebellion.
panelPlan: Single teaser splash at an industrial Shard challenge circle before any weapons are drawn, with Tess and Oren Pike opposite one another and divided adult captains as witnesses.
Preserve distinct Shard equipment, real arena geography, and the political character of the contest. The image must not depict the fight, an injury, its winner, or a fantasy gladiator setting.
Reserve disciplined empty space for the shorter scripted captions, with no extra environmental writing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT ISSUE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The convoy crossed. The corridor is still unexplained.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Seven captains followed Abby Saville instead of the Triarch.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now Shard command itself is being challenged.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Oren Pike wants Tess Banks in the circle.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: REX FLEET #8

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: KNIVES OUT.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic teaser only. Fear's certification campaign and the split command lead into Pike's political challenge. Do not pre-show the fight or its outcome. Preserve exact captions without adding slogans, signs or other readable text.
